title: Vowel Digraphs
keyIdea: A vowel digraph is two letters that make one vowel sound: ai in rain, ee in tree, oa in boat, oi in coin. Count sounds, not letters: r-ai-n has 4 letters but 3 sounds. Some sounds have two spellings: ai in the middle of a word, ay at the end (rain, play); oi in the middle, oy at the end (coin, boy). And one spelling can make two sounds: oo is long in moon and short in book.

kid: Some sounds need two letters. In rain, a and i make one sound: ai. Two letters, one sound.
So rain has 4 letters but 3 sounds: r-ai-n. Tree is t-r-ee. Boat is b-oa-t.
Where is the sound? In the middle we write ai or oi: rain, coin. At the end we write ay or oy: play, boy.
Listen to oo. In moon it is long. In book it is short. Same letters, two sounds.
adult: In England, phonics in Year 1 (National Curriculum 2014, Word Reading) asks children to respond speedily with the correct sound to graphemes for all 40+ phonemes, including alternative sounds for graphemes, and to read words containing taught GPCs. The Year 1 spelling appendix lists the vowel digraphs ai, oi, ay, oy, ee, ea, oa, oe and oo, and notes that ai and oi are virtually never used at the end of English words while ay and oy are used there. In the US, Common Core RF.1.3.c asks children to know final -e and common vowel team conventions for long vowel sounds.

Words to use: a grapheme is the letter or letters that write one sound (phoneme). A digraph is a grapheme of two letters; a vowel digraph (a vowel team) makes a vowel sound. Sound buttons show this: a dot under each single-letter grapheme and a line under a digraph. A phoneme frame has one box per sound, so coin needs 3 boxes, with oi sharing a box.

Common mistakes: sounding every letter (b-o-a-t, which gives four sounds and no word); spelling the end of play as plai; reading every oo as the long sound (so foot rhymes with boot); and thinking ee and ea must sound different. Be careful with ea: it usually says ee (sea, dream) but in some words it says a short e (head, bread), so check the word makes sense.

In the lab your child joins the two letters that make one sound and watches the sound buttons change, builds coin, seed and moon in phoneme frames, chooses ai or ay and oi or oy by where the gap sits, sorts oo words into moon or book, and posts words into sound houses for ee, ai and oa. Every drag has a button twin.

familyTip: Write a word like rain or boat on paper. Ask your child to draw a dot under each letter that makes its own sound and a line under the two letters that work together. Then count the sounds on fingers: r-ai-n, 3 sounds.

visual.caption: Which sound? Drag each word to a box, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: join two letters into one sound, fill phoneme frames, pick ai or ay by position, sort long and short oo, post words to sound houses.

practice.prompt: How many sounds are in the word boat?
practice.hint: Find the two letters that make one sound, then count sounds, not letters.
practice.explain: oa is a vowel digraph, so it is one sound: b-oa-t. That is 3 sounds from 4 letters.

practice.prompt: A word has {n} letters. Two of them make one sound together. Every other letter makes its own sound. How many sounds?
practice.hint: The two letters that work together count as just one sound.
practice.explain: {n} letters, but two of them share one sound, so the word has {=n-1} sounds. Rain: 4 letters, 3 sounds.

practice.prompt: Which spelling is right for the end of the word d_ (day)?
practice.hint: Is the gap in the middle of the word or at the end?
practice.explain: At the end of a word we usually write ay: day, play, say. ai goes in the middle: rain.

practice.prompt: Sam writes a word with {n} sounds. One of the sounds is a vowel digraph. How many letters does he write?
practice.hint: Each sound is one letter, except the digraph, which uses two.
practice.explain: {n} sounds need {n} graphemes. The digraph uses 2 letters, so there are {=n+1} letters, like s-ee-d.

pool.prompt: Which word has the same oo sound as book?
pool.hint: Say book. Is the oo short or long? Find the word with the short one.
pool.explain: book and foot both have the short oo. moon and spoon have the long oo.

pool.prompt: Which word is spelt the right way?
pool.hint: The sound is at the end of the word. Which spelling goes at the end?
pool.explain: oy usually goes at the end of a word: boy, toy. oi goes in the middle: coin.

pool.prompt: Which two spellings can both make the ee sound?
pool.hint: Think of tree and sea. Which letters make the ee sound in each?
pool.explain: ee in tree and ea in sea make the same sound. Some sounds have two spellings.

pool.prompt: In the word coin, which letters make one sound together?
pool.hint: Say coin slowly: c… then the middle sound… then n.
pool.explain: o and i make one sound, oi: c-oi-n. That is the vowel digraph.

pool.prompt: How many boxes does seed need in a phoneme frame?
pool.hint: One box for each sound, not each letter. Say s-ee-d.
pool.explain: seed has 3 sounds, s-ee-d, so it needs 3 boxes. ee shares one box.

pool.prompt: Which word has a long oo, like moon?
pool.hint: Say each word and stretch the oo. Which sounds like moon?
pool.explain: food has the long oo, like moon. good and look have the short oo, like book.

pool.prompt: Mia reads {n} words with ai and {k} words with ay. How many words with the ai sound did she read?
pool.hint: ai and ay both make the same sound. Add the two groups.
pool.explain: {n} words with ai and {k} with ay make {=n+k} words, all with the same ai sound.

pool.prompt: Which word has the same sound as toe?
pool.hint: oe in toe says oa. Which word has oa?
pool.explain: oe in toe and oa in boat make the same sound. boot has oo and bat has a short a.

pool.prompt: A word has {n} letters and one vowel digraph. A phoneme frame has one box for each sound. How many boxes does the word need?
pool.hint: The two letters of the digraph share one box. Every other letter gets its own box.
pool.explain: {n} letters, but the digraph's two letters share a box, so the frame needs {=n-1} boxes, like c-oi-n in 3 boxes.
